hook: SCP-514 is a flock of white homing pigeons, the kind people release at ceremonies, and wherever it flies, guns jam and tempers cool. It is one of the gentler entries you will find, written with a dry sense of humor that builds toward its last few lines. Pay attention to how the Foundation's own people behave whenever they get close to the birds.
whyItMatters: Most anomalies threaten people; this one threatens violence itself, and the file draws its tension from everyone who wants to use it anyway. Military officials and allied agencies are eager to turn a flock that dismantles weapons into a weapon, an irony the article lets you notice without underlining it. It also features the Manna Charitable Foundation, a charity group that crosses paths with the Foundation while both are tracking the birds.
thingsToNotice:
The test logs show the zone judging intent rather than objects: a steak knife and a baseball bat are left alone until someone holds them threateningly, while everything built to kill, down to a nuclear warhead that leaves no radiation behind, crumbles to dust within an hour. Violent D-class subjects calm down too, and the effect lingers for a time after they leave.

The discovery story undercuts the dream of peace. The charity released the birds in Africa to end conflict, but the calm wears off once the flock moves on and its random path disarmed only some regions, leaving them open to neighbors who were still armed. When the charity's team and the Foundation later fought over the flock and the control device, both sides were inside its zone, so the dispute was settled with one round of rock-paper-scissors, which the Foundation won.

Capture is impossible because every agent sent simply refuses the mission, so the final addendum orders the task force to train in sports, board games, trivia and rock-paper-scissors. An Overseer protests in disbelief, the captain promises they take it seriously, and O5-11 complains about grown men in black tactical gear treating a children's card game so solemnly.
